questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Practicing my language skills

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I wish I received more information from the university and in the intro week, as well as information about filling in the learning agreement.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much. I signed up for a buddy system where local students show around the international students and help them, but i was never contacted by one. All of the assistance was by e-mail by my tutor.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy and affordable. There are many Erasmus acommodation websites that also give you the opportunity to live with other Erasmus students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you haven't ever lived on your own, it can be very challenging, especially in a new country. But is is very fun to live with other international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to register.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got assigned a tutor that could assist me with academic help and choosing courses and filling in my learning agreement.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses I wanted, even though i did want to change one of them because it was too hard. I had the opportunity to do so, but didn't, because I was told it was a complicated process to change.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The first week does not matter. It is a good idea to attend every single course that you are interested in taking. And then you should pick the ones you find the most interesting and the professors seem nice and professional.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took 3 courses from the first year, 1 from the third year and 1 from the fourth year. They were on a different difficulty level, some seemed very hard and some were easier.
For me personally 5 courses in spanish which is my 5th language seemed very hard and was often worried that i didn't understand and would fail the exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. It seemed more old-school and it reminded me of how it is taught in upper-secondary school. There was no need for preparation for the lectures, but you were expected to participate actively in the practical classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
HISTORIA DE LAS IDEAS ESTÉTICAS
TEORÍA DE LA LITERATURA Y LITERATURA COMPARADA
TIPOS DE DISCURSO EN ESPAÑOL
ESPAÑOL DE AMÉRICA
ESPAÑOL NORMATIVO II

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend ESPAÑOL DE AMÉRICA because the teacher is very passionate about this class and i have learned a lot about the Spanish language in Latin America and the cultural difference between the two continents.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The university merch was more expensive, as well as buying groceries.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are many opportunities for free time by the university like hikes, movie screenings and ESN parties.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Same answer as above.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going to the ESN events like beach day, the parties and communal dinners because they are a great opportunity to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to nearby cities and explore the region.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very hard in the start, especially regarding meal time, but eventually i adapted my everyday life to be like a local spaniard.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Ask for help in class or go out and approach them at bars and parties.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the meal time difference, the siesta culture and the fact that everything is closed on Sundays.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Spanish people love their culture, their food and they show it. I absolutely loves fiestas de primavera and bando de la huerta.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is a big plus if you are fluent in spanish, as locals don't speak english very well. Beware of the murcian accent, which can be hard to understand at first.
It is a very small campus and everyone basically knows each other. So it is very easy to meet other erasmus students.
Choose the courses you find the most interesting and easy.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my language skills and gaining many friendships from different parts of the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Studying for the exams. You are not given a "læse ferie" like in UCPH, you have about 2 days for each exam to study.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
